intervals.label: MINOS far detector hall in operation
intervals.locator: MINOS detector paper §1, arXiv PDF p. 10 (start); end date from the Fermilab newsroom item of 2016-08
intervals.note: Start is the date the MINOS far detector became fully operational underground; end is the day the MINOS/MINOS+ runs concluded.
intervals.quote: has been fully operational for cosmic-ray and atmospheric-neutrino data since July 2003

intervals.label: decommissioning
intervals.note: The University of Minnesota page (last modified 2012-01-10) says the facility "is being decommissioned as existing experiments finish and new experiments go into newer, deeper facilities"; the MINOS/MINOS+ run ended on 2016-06-29. No official closure date was published in any source fetched, so no end date is asserted.
intervals.quote: being decommissioned as existing experiments finish and new experiments go into newer, deeper facilities

name: Soudan Underground Laboratory

summary.plain: A laboratory dug into a disused iron mine in northern Minnesota, about 700 metres below ground. The rock above it screens out most of the particles raining down from the sky, which let it host the far detector of the MINOS neutrino experiment and a dark matter search.
summary.technical: University of Minnesota underground facility in the Soudan iron mine at 705 m depth (2070 m.w.e.), host of the 5.4 kt MINOS far detector (2003-2016) and, on the same level, the CDMS II cryogenic dark matter experiment.
